main_text.l: latere, Ex omni parte: מִצַּד Ratione, propter: מִצַּד שׁ Eo-ut, Eo quòd, Propterea quod: מִצָּדוֹ Ex parte ejus, בְּאֵיזֶה צַד Quodam modo: כְּיֵצַד Quomodo: Nam, Nempe: בְּצַד Juxta: בְּצַדָּם Juxta te: Plur. צְדָדִים Latera, Modi. מִשְׁפָּט צִדְדִי Propositio modalis.

צְדַק, צֶדֶק Jupiter planeta. צְדָקָה Eleemosyna. דַּאֲיּוּר [?] Rationes justæ, certæ, legitimæ, verae. וְאַחַר כֵּן Postea declarabis vel distinguES legitimum sive verum ab illegitimo, sive falso. Rabbi Levi, Proverb. 2. ab initio. הַקְּדָמוֹת צִדְקוֹת Præmissæ veræ, quibus opponuntur כּוֹזְבוֹת Falsæ. צִדְקִיּוֹת Justæ, probæ mulieres.
צָהֹב Splendere, Rutilare ut aurum: פְּדָחַת מְאִירָה וּמְצֻחֶבֶת Frons lucens & splendens, R. Sal. Eccl.12.2. מְצֻהָּבֶת Inauratum: צָהֹב Aureus color, Aurum.

צָוַר Præcipere, Imperare. צִוּוּי Præceptum: Imperativus modus, apud Grammaticos. נְצְטַוּוּ Præcipi, Mandari, בְּמִצְוָּה Mandato, Jussu, Licentia N. in titulis librorum. בֵּר מִצְוָּה Filius præcepti, h.e. tredecim annorum; Gen.17. Aben Esra.

צִיר צוּר Formare, Designare. צוּר Formari: צוּרָה Forma, Figura. צִיּוּר Formatio, Figura, Pictura, Imaginatio: צַיָּר Formator, Figurator, Pictor: מְצַיֵּר Idem: בּוֹחַ הַמְּצִיר Facultas figurativa, Imaginativa: מְצוּיָר Efformatum, Figuratum.

צָחַח Candidum, Nitidum, Splendidum esse. צְחוֹת Nitor; Elegantia sermonis. לְדַבֵּר צְחוֹת Loqui nitida, elegantia verba, Jesa. 32.4. מְצֻחְצָח Idem. מְצוּחְצָח Splendens, Nitens, Pellucidum, Illustre, Lucidum.
צָחַק Ludere: מְלָאכֶת הַצְּחוּק Ars lusoria: צַחְקָן Lusor.
צִיֵּן Signare, Designare. צִיּוּן Signum, Circumscriptio, Delineatio: Monimentum sepulchrale, Epitaphium.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and several Hebrew words are not fully legible at this scan resolution and are given from best reading; they are not certain. The first line ends "Ed", read as the start of Eo-ut continued on the next line; the hyphen is inferred. In the entry "Postea declarabis", "distinguES" is a probable misreading and should be checked against the scan. The running head is a Hebrew letter, not a title. The signature at the foot is doubtful. The first Hebrew word in the second paragraph is uncertain.
